detail.title: Nonreciprocal Coupling and Coarse-Grained Dissipation Bounds
detail.summary: Thermodynamic dissipation in nonequilibrium systems is fundamentally linked to the information-processing capacity of the system. While generalized thermodynamic uncertainty relations (TURs) provide essential bounds, recent peer research suggests that control-theoretic approaches and the rigorous separation of causal laws from statistical correlations are necessary to prevent the overestimation of dissipation limits in multi-level physical systems.
detail.reason: Revision necessary to integrate new peer research on passive controller efficiency and causal validity, directly addressing the ambiguity in current dissipation bounds.
